summary: Peter von Bohlen was an Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Bonn, and Berlin under Georg Wilhelm Freytag, August Wilhelm von Schlegel, and Franz Bopp. He served as professor of oriental literature at the University of Königsberg starting in 1825.

Peter von Bradke was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Dorpat/Tartu under Leo Meyer, at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and at Leipzig, Jena, and Giessen, later becoming an außerordentlicher Professor at Giessen (1886–1896).

Peter von Köppen worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the National University of Kharkiv (ca. 1810–1814) and the University of Tübingen (ca. 1822–1823), later serving in the Ministry of State Property from ca. 1837 to 1852.

Petra Kieffer-Pülz is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Heinz Bechert. She held posts at the University of Göttingen (attested 1995), Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz (ca. 2000), and the Pali Text Society (ca. 2018).

Petra Maurer is a Tibetologist and Indologist who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She has held posts at the University of Munich, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Phakchok Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his Khenpo title at Dzongsar Institute (ca. 1997–2004), studied under numerous traditional teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and served as Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling.
Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Maha Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull.

Phanit Jetjiravat is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under academic advisors Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown, and served as Associate Professor at the University of Chicago (1963–1978) before becoming Francis Lee Higginson Professor and Fairbank Center director at Harvard.

Philip A. Mellor is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester by 1989 and served as Professor and Head of the School of Humanities at the University of Leeds (attested 2010).

Philip B. Yampolsky was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at Columbia University and under Yoshitaka Iriya, he served as Columbia's East Asian Library librarian and Japanese lecturer, and chaired the Numata Center (1991–1996).

Philip Clart is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied under Daniel L. Overmyer from ca. 1990 to 1996 and was appointed Professor of Chinese Culture and History at Leipzig University in ca. 2008.

Philip Deslippe is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He has been a graduate student (attested 2020–2026) and teaching associate (attested 2020) at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Philip Kapleau was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Soen Nakagawa, Daiun Sogaku Harada, and Hakuun Yasutani. He founded the Rochester Zen Center and Chapin Mill Retreat Center.

Philip L. Quinn was a philosopher who studied at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He taught at Brown University (ca. 1976–1985), served as John A. O'Brien Professor of Philosophy at Notre Dame from 1985, and presided over the APA (1994–1995).

Philip Lutgendorf is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago (ca. 1967–1987), joined the University of Iowa faculty in 1985, and served as President of the American Institute of Indian Studies (2010–2018).

Philip Novak is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Syracuse University and the University of Notre Dame. He became a teacher at Dominican University of California around 1980.

Philip T. Denwood is a Tibetologist and linguist who held posts at SOAS University of London, including Lecturer in Tibetan starting in 1965 and Reader in the Department of Art & Archaeology (attested 2005).

Philip Whalen was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Reed College and under Richard Baker. He served as head monk at Dharma Sangha (1984), resident teacher at South Ridge Zendo, and abbot at Hartford Street Zen Center (1991).

Philipp André Maas is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler. He has held positions at Bonn, the University of Vienna, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and Leipzig University.
